result.title: Interpretable structural temperature scaling for calibrating graph neural networks and point-cloud segmentation
result.comment: Under consideration at Pattern Recognition Letters. 7 pages, 6 tables, 1 figure; supplementary material in ancillary files
result.summary: Graph-aware calibrators make graph neural networks (GNNs) more trustworthy by predicting a temperature for each node, usually with auxiliary networks whose decisions are hard to inspect. We propose Interpretable Structural Temperature Scaling (ISTS), a twelve-parameter linear model that sets each node's temperature from named descriptors of its confidence, neighbourhood and closeness to labelled nodes, so every temperature traces back to descriptor contributions. ISTS preserves predictions, and cross-validated regularisation lets the calibration data decide how far the model departs from temperature scaling (TS). Its explanations are faithful at the level of node groups: on test nodes, ISTS softens groups that a global temperature leaves over-confident and sharpens under-confident ones (Spearman correlation 0.67 over 246 groups). On seven graphs with two backbones and eleven baselines, ISTS has the best average rank in negative log-likelihood (NLL) and Brier score and lowers NLL relative to TS by 1.8%, more than twice the gain of an identically fitted entropy-based temperature. It ranked first again on four held-out graphs under a protocol fixed in advance. From about 100 calibration nodes on, ISTS is a cheap and inspectable choice, and on point-cloud segmentation it significantly improves NLL, Brier score and the ranking of points for rejection.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ISTS：一个十二参数线性模型，依据节点置信度、邻域结构和与标注节点的接近度等可命名描述子为每个节点设定温度，实现可追溯的 GNN 与点云分割后校准，并保留原预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐元素、可解释的置信度校准，可能为 LVR 中「何时停止取证据/停止推理」提供廉价的不确定性信号，且其邻域描述子与状态/关系建模有概念类比，但论文本身不涉及 latent 推理，迁移价值需核查。
